summary: Sony's analog-stick platform and party series; use modern PlayStation classics for the first two main games, emulation for PS2/PSP-only entries, and original hardware for EyeToy/Move releases.

entries.title: Ape Escape

emulation.notes: Original PlayStation release requires dual analog controls.

primary.why: The modern PlayStation release preserves the original DualShock-focused PlayStation game while adding official up-rendering, rewind, quick save, and video filters.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS4/PS5 PlayStation Store release; use DuckStation only for original-disc comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Modern release is an enhanced classic rather than a remake.

emulation.notes: Use a Japanese release; no official English release documented.

primary.why: Pipo Saru 2001 is a Japan-only PS2 spin-off with no modern port documented; PCSX2 gives the best practical fidelity for the original release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution, or on Japanese/region-compatible PS2 hardware.

entries.title: Ape Escape 2

emulation.notes: PCSX2 can upscale the PS2 disc if the PS4 release is unavailable.

primary.why: The PS4 release is the official modern version of the PS2 game and adds up-rendering and trophies.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS4 PlayStation Store release, playable on PS5 via backward compatibility where available; use PCSX2 as a fallback for the PS2 disc.

entries.remaster_caveats: Converted PS2 titles may play differently and may not support PS2 peripherals.

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for high-resolution PSP playback.

primary.why: On the Loose is the PSP remake/version of the first Ape Escape and has no modern port documented; PPSSPP is the best practical fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP release through PPSSPP at high internal resolution, or on PSP hardware.

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for high internal resolution.

primary.why: Pumped & Primed is a PS2-only party spin-off released in Japan and North America; PCSX2 gives the best practical fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution, or on original PS2 hardware.

primary.why: Monkey Mania is a PS2 EyeToy party game that requires the camera peripheral, so original hardware is the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PS2 hardware with an EyeToy camera; emulation is not the recommended main route because the peripheral is central to play.

emulation.notes: Original hardware is preferred for authentic local wireless play.

primary.why: Ape Escape Academy is a PSP-only minigame collection; PPSSPP offers the highest practical fidelity for single-player preservation.
primary.how_to_play: Play through PPSSPP at high internal resolution; use PSP hardware for original local wireless multiplayer conditions.

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for high internal resolution.

primary.why: Ape Escape 3 is a PS2-only mainline entry with no released modern port documented; PCSX2 gives the best practical fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution, or on original PS2 hardware.

emulation.notes: Use original PSP hardware for authentic local multiplayer.

primary.why: Ape Academy 2 is a PSP-only sequel released in Japan and Europe; PPSSPP offers the best practical fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP release through PPSSPP; use original PSP hardware for local multiplayer.

emulation.notes: Use the original regional release; no North American release documented.

primary.why: Million Monkeys is a PS2-only Ape Escape platform/action entry that was released in Asia and canceled elsewhere; PCSX2 is the best practical fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Asia/Japan PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution, or on compatible PS2 hardware.

entries.title: Saru Get You: Pipo Saru Racer

primary.why: Pipo Saru Racer is a Japan-only PSP racing spin-off with no modern port documented; PPSSPP gives the best practical fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese PSP release through PPSSPP at high internal resolution, or on PSP hardware.

entries.title: Saru! Get You! SaruSaru Big Mission

primary.why: SaruSaru Big Mission is a Japan-only PSP spin-off with no modern port documented; PPSSPP gives the best practical fidelity.

emulation.notes: Verify full chapter content, not just the starter pack.

primary.why: Ape Quest is a PSP RPG spin-off released digitally in North America/Europe and on UMD in Japan; PPSSPP gives the best preservation fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP release through PPSSPP at high internal resolution; ensure the full chapter content is available, not only the free starter pack.

emulation.notes: Requires PlayStation Move controller and camera.

primary.why: This PS3 spin-off is built around PlayStation Move motion controls, so original PS3 hardware with the Move setup is the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PS3 hardware with PlayStation Move controller and camera; emulation is not the recommended main route because motion controls are central.
